warning_source: State Comptroller Matanyahu Englman / Office of the State Comptroller
recipient: Benjamin Netanyahu; Yoav Gallant; Herzi Halevi; political-security cabinet
warning_summary: Northern-border flash audit documented serious readiness, barrier, intelligence, patrol and outpost-defense gaps amid rising Hezbollah activity.
evidence_update: The declassified official recommendation section was added to the Notion entry: it explicitly urged the Prime Minister and political-security cabinet to assess Lebanon/Hezbollah noncompliance with UNSCR 1701 and determine policy, and urged the Chief of Staff to reassess Blue Line force posture and operational means given rising threats since early 2023, Hezbollah proximity and barrier weak points. High-confidence primary-document upgrade; no new warning event.
gaps: Exact 14 Aug delivery date still rests on secondary reporting; official Comptroller material confirms August delivery. No causal inference to Oct. 7.

warning_source: Moshe Davidovich / Confrontation Line Forum, with northern-border mayors
recipient: Yoav Gallant / Defense Ministry; Netanyahu government; Prime Minister's Office / DG Yossi Shelley
warning_summary: Local leaders warned that cuts and delays in Shield of the North left thousands of northern-border residents exposed to Hezbollah attack and risked loss of life.
evidence_update: A contemporaneous 6 Jun 2023 local report reproducing a PMO DG Yossi Shelley reply says the PMO requested urgent documents from the forum for preparation of a government decision. Davidovich's contemporaneous response warned that reduced protection funding left residents exposed and without required state protection and risked loss of life. Added to WARN-64 as direct institutional-receipt evidence for the continuing warning chain, not a duplicate event.
gaps: The recovered PMO correspondence strengthens institutional receipt but does not prove Gallant personally read the original 15 Mar warning; confidence remains Medium. Original underlying urgent-document package has not been recovered.

warning_source: Bini Kfir, commander of Moshav Tkuma standby squad
recipient: Unnamed senior Gaza-area officer; previous brigade commander; regional-council heads
warning_summary: Kfir says he repeatedly warned that Tkuma's standby squad could not function after weapons were removed and that a senior officer dismissed the concern because the Gaza barrier eliminated the threat.
evidence_update: Ynet preserves Kfir's retrospective account and the text he says he sent to regional-council heads. A later official IDF History Department study independently corroborates the broader erosion of standby-squad weapons/training and the barrier-driven security conception, but also states there was no authorized blanket order requiring 0–4 km communities to store weapons in armories; written directives generally called for weapons to remain with squad members, while practice varied locally. This materially strengthens structural context while qualifying Kfir's description of an army-wide weapon-removal policy.
gaps: Specific pre-Oct. 7 warning date, named senior recipient and contemporaneous Kfir letter/message remain unrecovered. Same-witness retrospective retellings are not independent event-level corroboration. Keep Investigating.
